ABSTRACT: Confinement of hydrocarbons in nanoscale pockets and pores provides tunable capability for controlling molecules in catalysts, sorbents, and membranes for reaction and separation applications. While computation of the enthalpic interactions of hydrocarbons in confined spaces has improved, understanding and predicting the entropy of confined molecules remains a challenge. Here we show, using a set of nine aluminosilicate zeolite frameworks with broad variation in pore and cavity structure, that the entropy of adsorption can be predicted as a linear combination of rotational and translational entropy. The extent of entropy lost upon adsorption is predicted using only a single material descriptor, the occupiable volume ( $ V_{occ} $). Predictive capability of confined molecular entropy permits an understanding of the relation with adsorption enthalpy, the ability to computationally screen microporous materials, and an understanding of the role of confinement on the kinetics of molecules in confined spaces.

On the basis of this shape-selective feature , highly effective molecular separations and selective catalytic conversions can be achieved within zeolitic structures that are difficult to accomplish with other materials and/or techniques . $ ^ { 1-3 } $ So far, several shape-selectivity mechanisms have been elucidated and applications identified. $ ^{2-18} $ In common molecular sieving, bulky molecules adsorb preferentially over bulkier species as a result of steric constraints imposed by the zeolites' framework, e.g., linear alkane molecules compared to branched isomers. $ ^{19-23} $ Besides this common adsorption competition based on molecular bulkiness, the reverse phenomenon can also occur, i.e., competitive adsorption in favor of the bulkier species. Experiments revealed preferential adsorption of branched alkanes over their linear isomers on specific zeolites with tubular pore systems such as SAPO-5 and Mordenite. $ ^{24-28} $ Molecular simulations indicated that in such zeolites, depending on conditions, branched alkanes are preferentially adsorbed at the expense of linear isomers. $ ^{29-34} $ The present manuscript discusses the mechanisms of shape selectivity in n- and isoalkane adsorption on zeolite MCM-22. This zeolite with IZA code MWW is a relatively new synthetic material that has an unusual and quite complex pore structure. $ ^{35} $ Its framework is composed of two independent pore systems. The enthalpy and the entropy contributions to the Gibbs free energies were calculated at T = 298 K and partial pressure of 1 atm (101325 Pa). The enthalpy (H) of gas-phase pyridine and acetonitrile molecules is defined as the sum of total electronic energy ( $ E_{el} $), internal vibrational energy ( $ E_{v} $), zero-point vibrational energy (ZPVE), as well as the rotational and translational contributions to the internal energy: $ H = E_{el} + E_{v} + ZPVE + E_{R} + E_{t} $. The corresponding calculated entropies (S) includes translational, ( $ S_{t} $) vibrational, ( $ S_{v} $) and rotational ( $ S_{r} $) degrees of freedom: $ S = S_{t} + S_{v} + S_{r} $. All the considered systems are in singlet state, thus the electronic contribution to the entropy is zero. Since both adsorbed molecules are constrained in the zeolite cavity their entropy contributions in the adsorption complexes were corrected as follows: the translational and rotational degrees of freedom were reduced by 1 and 1.28 [37]. 1.2.1. Framework dynamics. The first attempts to describe guest-induced flexibility in zeolites were done using molecular dynamics simulations. $ ^{79-82} $ Rigid zeolitic force fields were dynamically modified using transition state theory to include lattice flexibility, and the results obtained by these models were in good agreement with experimental data. $ ^{79-81,83,84} $ It was shown that framework flexibility in silicalite-1 (MFI-type framework) is responsible for the adsorption of large molecules such as isobutane and heptane with inflection behavior at high loadings, $ ^{80} $ while enhanced self-diffusivity at low loadings of short alkanes (i.e. methane and n-butane) was observed. $ ^{81} $ Framework flexibility is also crucial for aromatics adsorption on MFI zeolite, especially at high pressures. $ ^{84,85} $ While the use of rigid zeolitic models led to the underestimation of the aromatics adsorption in MFI zeolite by a factor of two, $ ^{84,85} $ the use of flexible models to simulate diffusion coefficients of various alkanes in silicalite-1 zeolite resulted in a convergence of experimental and theoretical values. $ ^{86} $ Recently by using in situ integrated differential phase contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy (iDPC-STEM) while adsorbing benzene molecules on MFI zeolite, Xiong et al. showed that the MFI structure goes through severe deformations giving another proof of guest-induced flexibility in zeolites (see Fig. 4). $ ^{87} $

2.4.4. Trapdoor. Traditional diﬀusion models primarily consider two types of interactions: those between guest molecules (guest–guest) and those between guest molecules and the zeolite framework (guest–host). However, when cations are present in the zeolite structure, a third interaction—involving guest molecules, the framework, and cations (guest–host-cation)—must also be accounted for. A striking example of such ternary interactions is the well-known ‘‘molecular trapdoor’’. This phenomenon, also referred to as the ‘‘gating effect’’, describes a unique molecular sieving mechanism in certain zeolites and related porous materi- als. Here, extra-framework cations function as dynamic gate- keepers at pore apertures, selectively controlling molecular diffusion to achieve highly discriminative adsorption and separation.9,147,187 To date, ‘‘trapdoor’’ has been observed in several zeolites, including RHO (DNL-6),188–190 CHA (SAPO-34, SSZ-13),147,191,192 MWF (ZSM-25),149,193 HEU (Clinoptilolite),194

descriptor_candidates.name: conf_ratio_geom
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Replacing the raw occupiable-volume scaling with a ratio of molecular volume to framework pore volume (AV weighted by source density) reduces MAE of entropy loss/R relative to the published 14-input model, because entropy loss is governed by the molecule-to-pore confinement ratio, not either quantity alone.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Confinement entropy loss scales with how completely the guest fills the pore: small molecule in large cage (FAU) loses little entropy; molecule comparable to channel diameter (TON) loses most. The ratio encodes this shape-matching mechanism.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If adding this single descriptor (replacing AV or Vol in the nonlinear network) does not reduce MAE of S_loss/R versus the full 14-input baseline on held-out zeolite/adsorbate pairs, the confinement-ratio hypothesis is falsified for this dataset.

descriptor_candidates.name: shape_anisotropy_confinement
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Adsorption entropy loss increases with molecular shape anisotropy (PMI3/PMI1) modulated by the mismatch between molecular span and the largest pore diameter; a descriptor combining both predicts entropy loss better than any size-only descriptor, because elongated molecules in narrow channels lose rotational freedom while near-spherical molecules in cavities retain it.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Rotational entropy loss depends on anisotropy of the moment-of-inertia tensor relative to channel geometry (E01 distinguishes translational vs rotational contributions; E09 shows molecular symmetry alters confined dynamics). Span-to-pore-diameter mismatch measures steric restriction of rotation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the descriptor's partial effect on predicted S_loss/R is not monotonic in PMI3/PMI1 at fixed pore size (tested via sensitivity analysis on the trained network), or if MAE does not improve over a volume-only control, the anisotropy mechanism is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: accessible_surface_fraction
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: The fraction of molecular surface accessible within the framework (molecular ASA-type descriptor times a pore-length-scale weighting) captures the immobilization of translational degrees of freedom; entropy loss per R correlates negatively with this accessible-surface fraction and the descriptor improves MAE over pore-volume-only descriptors because adsorbed molecules retain more entropy when contact area with pore walls is small.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Sackur-Tetrode translational loss (E01) is larger when the molecule is immobilized over a large wall-contact area; lsd_f and lsd_p characterize free-sphere vs pore-limited diameters, so their combination with molecular surface area estimates the degree of wall-contact constriction.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the descriptor fails to outperform a randomized-permutation control of the same inputs (no MAE reduction on validation), or if its fitted partial dependence shows no negative relation to S_loss/R, the wall-contact immobilization hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: pore_window_tortuosity
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Adsorption entropy loss/R increases when the free-sphere pore diameter (lsd_f) deviates upward from the actual pore-limited diameter (lsd_p), indicating constricted or window-limited diffusion paths; multiplying this window-constriction factor by the molecule-to-pore volume ratio (in log form, extending the round-1 confinement ratio) improves MAE of S_loss/R over the 14-input baseline, because narrow windows between larger cages force partial translational immobilization even when cage volume is large.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01: frameworks with cage-like topologies (FAU) show small entropy loss while channel frameworks (TON) show large loss, so window-to-free-diameter ratio encodes the channel vs cage distinction that occupiable volume alone misses. E05 supports shape/diameter-matching selectivity at pore windows.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If adding this descriptor does not reduce MAE of entropy loss/R on held-out zeolite/adsorbate pairs versus the published 14-input baseline, or if its partial dependence on lsd_f/lsd_p is not monotonic in sensitivity analysis, the window-constriction hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: surface_bulky_packing
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: The ratio of molecular surface area to the surface of a sphere of equal volume (shape sphericity proxy) predicts entropy loss: molecules with high surface-to-volume-shape ratio (elongated/branched) lose more entropy per unit confinement than compact molecules at equal volume, and this descriptor improves MAE beyond the retained anisotropy descriptor because it captures branching independently of the inertia tensor.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01 and E05: linear and branched alkane isomers have equal volumes but different entropy losses and adsorption behavior; surface-area-to-diameter ratio distinguishes branching without using PMI, testing whether the anisotropy mechanism generalizes or is specific to inertia-based encoding.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If this descriptor shows no partial correlation with the retained shape_anisotropy_confinement descriptor's residuals and no MAE improvement over the round-2 retained model, the branching-as-separate-mechanism claim is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: framework_dense_cavity_index
descriptor_candidates.formula: log(AV + 1) * (1 - minimum(1, density / maximum(1.8, 1.8))) + (1 - ASA / (ASA + 500)) * GeDi
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R increases with framework geometric diameter (GeDi) only when framework density indicates a densely packed structure; a term combining GeDi with density-based packing correction predicts the cage-size effect better than GeDi or AV alone, because large cavities in dense frameworks (e.g., small-pore window cages) confine rotation more than the same cavities in open frameworks.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01: framework identity, not molecular volume alone, controls entropy loss; framework density (source numerical scale) is a topology proxy distinguishing dense vs open frameworks among pure-silica structures, and GeDi encodes cavity diameter. Their product tests whether topology modulates the cavity-size effect.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If interaction analysis shows the partial effect of GeDi on predicted S_loss/R does not change sign or magnitude across the density range present in the dataset, or if MAE does not improve over the baseline, the topology-modulation hypothesis is falsified for this dataset.

descriptor_candidates.name: asphericity_pore_match
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R increases when the molecular 'maximum-brim' radius (PBF) is large relative to the cube-root of its volume (a prolate/elongation measure) and the molecule fills a large fraction of the pore volume; the product of these two factors improves MAE of entropy loss/R over the 14-input baseline because elongation and confinement jointly suppress rotational and vibrational freedom of the adsorbed phase.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01: entropy loss differs by framework at fixed molecule, implying a confinement-ratio mechanism; E05 shows shape matching at pore windows alters adsorption states. PBF/Vol^(1/3) encodes elongation without the inertia tensor (complementing the retained PMI descriptor), while the volume-filling ratio encodes cage-vs-channel degree of confinement. This is a re-expression of existing inputs, not a verified discovery.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If adding this descriptor to the nonlinear network does not reduce MAE of S_loss/R on held-out zeolite/adsorbate pairs versus the published 14-input baseline, or if its partial dependence on PBF/Vol^(1/3) is non-monotonic in sensitivity analysis at fixed confinement ratio, the joint elongation-filling hypothesis is falsified for this dataset.

descriptor_candidates.name: window_gap_crowding
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R rises with molecular volume multiplied by the fractional window constriction (1 - lsd_p/lsd_f) and weighted by the cavity-to-window contrast (GeDi vs lsd_f): large molecules entering big cavities through narrow windows are translationally immobilized at the window and vibrationally damped in the cage, so this crowding term predicts S_loss/R better than the retained surface-packing descriptor.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01: FAU (large cages) gives the smallest loss and TON (narrow channels) the largest, suggesting window/cavity contrast, not cage size alone, controls entropy loss; E05 documents steric constraints at pore openings. The constriction factor distinguishes 'big cage, tight window' from 'open channel' topologies using only lsd_f, lsd_p, GeDi and Vol. Source evidence supports topology dependence; the specific formula is inferred, not established.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the descriptor does not reduce MAE of S_loss/R versus the retained round-2 model, or if sensitivity analysis shows no monotonic increase of predicted S_loss/R with (1 - lsd_p/lsd_f) at fixed Vol, the window-crowding hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: density_gravity_compaction
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R increases with the square root of molecular mass (a Sackur-Tetrode translational-entropy proxy, since S_trans scales with (3/2)ln m), amplified in frameworks of high density and when the molecular span exceeds the pore-limited diameter; this compactness-steric term improves MAE over the retained descriptors because it couples the mass-driven gas-phase entropy ceiling to how completely the span is sterically clamped.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Source evidence (E01) gives the Sackur-Tetrode form showing gas-phase translational entropy grows with mass, setting the entropy budget available for loss; framework-dependent loss (E01) and shape matching (E05) motivate the density and span-clamp modulators. The mass dependence is a known_relation; the interaction with density and span clamping is an inferred new combination, not a verified discovery.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the descriptor's marginal improvement over the round-2 retained model is not positive on held-out data, or if its partial dependence on sqrt(MW) is flat within each framework subgroup in sensitivity analysis, the mass-times-steric-clamp hypothesis is falsified.
